posts.note: Personal essay on turning 45. Only aphorisms about aging and mortality ('life gets worse until you die', 'the death rate is holding constant at 100%'); treated as truisms and not logged.
COMP360 (Compass Pathways) PTSD phase 2 top-line data. One expectation of phase 3 trials and one hope-framed call; the rest is description of the data and of PTSD.
Satirical vampire dialogue about the Change Healthcare ransomware attack and private equity roll-ups. All three items are inside the satire and flagged sincere=false.

Evidence review of cannabis for PTSD; almost all past analysis. One pipeline statement (MDMA at FDA, psilocybin analogs, magnesium-ibogaine) logged as borderline. 'More Breakthroughs, please' is a wish and not logged.
Review of GLP-1 drugs in substance use disorders. One hedged efficacy signal and one general mechanistic expectation; calls to volunteer for trials are normative and not logged.
Review of a Japanese rTMS registry paper. One joke about robots and one 'key market' inference. Demands for payer coverage of TMS are normative and not logged.
Conference dispatch on food as medicine. One metaphor about GLP-1s versus Big Sugar logged as borderline; 'More soon!' sign-off not logged.
Part III on the Lykos MDMA-AT FDA advisory committee. Includes the subtitle conditional; quoted public commenters' claims are third-party and not logged.

Part IV on MDMA-AT: prior authorization prediction, need for safeguards, path to market, and a newsletter content promise. Trial-design recommendations (binary endpoints, MDMA-naive enrollment) are normative and not logged.
Response to Surgeon General Murthy's NY Times op-ed on a social media warning label. Two backfire predictions, one in sarcastic framing.

statements.quote: We don't have the published studies yet, we're just getting results at 12 weeks after the conclusion of the phase 2 trial for COMP360. However, here is what it looks like, and I really look forward to the results in subsequent phase 3 trials.
statements.context: Compass Pathways released 12-week top-line phase 2 data on COMP360 (psilocybin) for PTSD (mean CAPS-5 reduction about 30 points, over half in remission). The author expects the program to proceed to phase 3 trials and anticipates their results.
statements.note: Implicit call that the COMP360 PTSD program advances to phase 3; no stated direction for the phase 3 result.

statements.quote: If we lost our way, I hope this may be rediscovering a road back to healing.
statements.context: After the COMP360 PTSD phase 2 data, the author hopes psilocybin-type compounds may become a route to healing trauma. The next sentence adds that science must still determine for whom the treatment is most appropriate.
statements.note: Hope-framed; borderline wish rather than a call.

statements.quote: They know who all of us are, and they're coming for us.
statements.context: Satirical 'all-fangs meeting for vampires' about the Change Healthcare ransomware breach and private equity roll-ups. In the analogy the stolen blood is protected health information; the vampire narrator warns that the hunters (those holding the data) know everyone and are coming.
statements.note: Satirical vampire dialogue; the real-world referent (fallout from the Change Healthcare breach) is implied but not stated.

statements.quote: I am similarly concerned. I am assured that if we pay the ransom, the consequences will be mitigated.
statements.context: Same satirical vampire dialogue on the Change Healthcare ransomware attack. The narrator relays an assurance from unnamed others that paying the ransom mitigates the consequences; the ironic tone signals doubt.
statements.note: Conditional relayed as others' assurance inside satire; the author's own stance appears skeptical.

statements.quote: Instead of a stake through the heart, they use holy water if you pay the ransom.
statements.context: Closing line of the satirical vampire dialogue about the Change Healthcare ransomware attack: paying the ransom changes the form of the harm but does not remove it.
statements.note: Joke; the underlying claim is that paying the ransom still leaves the payer harmed.

statements.quote: It doesn't escape anybody's notice that MDMA is going through the FDA-approval process with Lykos Therapeutics, and other hopeful publications are coming out. These include psilocybin analogs for PTSD, and magnesium-ibogaine for PTSD.
statements.context: Closing section of a review that finds the cannabis evidence for PTSD weak and biased. The author points to a pipeline of hopeful PTSD treatments: MDMA under FDA review with Lykos, psilocybin analogs, and magnesium-ibogaine, with publications 'coming out'.
statements.note: Mostly a pipeline description; weak forward-looking reading via 'hopeful' and 'coming out'.

statements.quote: we can understand that biological treatments intervening in this crucial structure will have a hard time getting it to accomplish anything other than what it's biologically attuned to.
statements.context: Setup for a review of GLP-1 drugs in addiction. The 'crucial structure' is the nucleus accumbens; the author expects biological addiction treatments that act on reward circuitry to struggle to change what it does.

statements.quote: We have a signal—that's what we call noticing in science—that GLP-1s might be helpful for addictions.
statements.context: Review of GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide, liraglutide, exenatide) in substance use disorders. Evidence is mostly preclinical plus small human signals; human trials such as SEMALCO are recruiting. The author reads the signal as hedged promise pending trials.
statements.note: Hedged efficacy call; the author adds that current evidence does not support treating primary addiction with these drugs yet.

statements.quote: I welcome our robot overlords, but I think it's pretty clear that the humans are dead over any reasonable time frame.
statements.context: Aside while reviewing Japanese attitudes toward robots (explicit preference, implicit fear). Joke about robots replacing humans.
statements.note: Joke; does not read as a real expectation.

statements.quote: This should be the key market for Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation.
statements.context: Japanese respondents are far more open to home-care robots than Irish or Finnish respondents. The author infers Japan should be the key market for TMS and adds that a robot-ish solution to depression 'would be a big deal' there, even though the post says TMS is underutilized in Japan today.
statements.note: 'Should' reads as expectation as much as recommendation; borderline.

statements.quote: sugar and pharma are now no longer in sync. GLP-1s are a shot across the bow
statements.context: Dispatch from the thINc360 food-as-medicine conference. The author says Big Sugar and pharma interests have diverged and GLP-1 drugs are an opening salvo against the sugar industry, citing South Park's 'The End of Obesity'.
statements.note: Metaphor implying a coming conflict between GLP-1 makers and the sugar industry; borderline.

statements.quote: Harms and misconduct will scale if they are allowed to train and certify therapists.
statements.context: Subtitle of Part III on the Lykos Therapeutics MDMA-assisted therapy FDA submission. 'They' is Lykos/MAPS PBC; the claim is that if the sponsor is allowed to train and certify MDMA-AT therapists, the harms and misconduct alleged in the trials will scale.
statements.note: Conditional on Lykos/MAPS training and certifying therapists after approval.

statements.quote: It may be one of the many purposeful decisions that may doom the submission, as it stands.
statements.context: The FDA advisory committee objected that Lykos did not record positive subjective drug effects in MDMA-AT sessions, against prior FDA advice. The author says this may be one of several decisions that doom the Lykos MDMA NDA as submitted.
statements.note: Hedged call that the Lykos MDMA-AT submission fails in its current form.

statements.quote: deeply disturbing claims that the FDA will now be forced to investigate
statements.context: Public comment at the June 2024 FDA advisory committee alleged unreported suicide attempts and adverse events in the MAPS/Lykos MDMA-AT trials. The author says the FDA will now be forced to investigate these claims.

statements.quote: The worst part of psychedelic medicine is yet to come. If you think it's bad now, just wait till there are prior authorization hoops to jump through!
statements.context: Opening of Part IV, after Stat News coverage of the Lykos/MAPS drama and of Elevance firing its CarelonRx PBM director. The author predicts payer prior authorization requirements will become the worst part of psychedelic medicine once it reaches the market.
statements.note: Presumes psychedelic medicines reach a commercial, payer-covered stage.

statements.quote: I strongly suspect we're going to need additional safeguards in place
statements.context: After the FDA open comment period and advisory committee on Lykos's MDMA-AT, the author expects additional safeguards will be needed to market a drug-plus-procedure combination safely; the article then proposes clinical trial design fixes.

statements.quote: None of this means that the underlying compounds being studied in clinical trials can’t be successfully studied and brought to market.
statements.context: Despite former MAPS employees describing cult-like tendencies at MAPS in Stat News, the author holds that psychedelic compounds such as MDMA can still be studied properly and brought to market, and outlines a path forward.
statements.note: Double-negative, possibility-level call that psychedelic compounds still reach the market.

statements.quote: Future instruments will address safety, monitoring, and the use of artificial intelligence in the study and commercial deployment plans.
statements.context: Closing of Part IV of the MDMA-AT series. The author promises future installments ('instruments' is a typo) on safety, monitoring, and AI in study and commercial deployment plans. A call about the author's own newsletter.

statements.quote: Reminding adolescents that something—Murthy’s proposed plan— isn’t safe? This is an awesome strategy to encourage more of that behavior.
statements.context: Response to Surgeon General Vivek Murthy's NY Times op-ed calling for a congressionally mandated warning label on social media. Sarcastic framing: the author predicts a warning label will backfire and increase adolescent social media use, citing approach sensitization and the antidepressant black-box warning precedent. Public health policy domain.
statements.note: Sarcasm carries a sincere backfire prediction; the earlier 'Of course all adolescents stop doing it' makes the same point inverted.

statements.quote: Perhaps we need a warning label on warning labels from regulators and surgeons general? Warning: Unintended Consequences May Follow.
statements.context: Close of the argument against Murthy's proposed social media warning label. The author expects unintended consequences from warning labels issued by regulators and surgeons general, drawing on the antidepressant boxed warning and tobacco label evidence. Public health policy domain.
